subject: Anatomy
topic: Carpal Tunnel Syndrome Median Nerve Compression & Palmar Sparing
stem: A 48-year-old female dental hygienist presents with numbness, tingling, and burning pain involving the palmar aspect of her right thumb, index, and middle fingers that wakes her up from sleep at night. Shaking her hand provides temporary relief. Physical examination reveals: Tinel sign positive at the volar wrist, Phalen maneuver reproducing paresthesias within 30 seconds, and mild atrophy of the right thenar eminence with weakness on resisted thumb abduction (abductor pollicis brevis). However, sensory pinprick testing reveals normal sensation over the central proximal thenar eminence. Which of the following anatomical descriptions correctly explains why sensation over the thenar eminence is preserved in this patient?

options.text: The superficial sensory branch of the radial nerve crosses over the anatomical snuffbox to provide collateral innervation to the thenar palm
options.explanation: The superficial radial nerve innervates the dorsum of the hand and dorsal thumb/index finger; it does not innervate the palmar thenar eminence.

options.text: The palmar cutaneous branch of the ulnar nerve supplies overlapping cross-innervation across the median-ulnar watershed zone
options.explanation: The palmar cutaneous branch of the ulnar nerve supplies the hypothenar eminence, not the thenar eminence.

options.text: The recurrent motor branch of the median nerve carries dual sensory-motor fibers that bypass the carpal tunnel via the canal of Guyon
options.explanation: The recurrent branch is purely motor to the thenar muscles (OAF: Opponens, Abductor, Flexor pollicis brevis superficial head); the canal of Guyon contains the ulnar nerve.

options.text: The palmar cutaneous branch of the median nerve arises proximal to the flexor retinaculum (transverse carpal ligament) and passes superficial to the carpal tunnel
options.explanation: The median nerve gives off the palmar cutaneous branch approximately 5 cm proximal to the wrist crease. This branch courses superficial to the flexor retinaculum (transverse carpal ligament) to innervate the skin overlying the central thenar eminence. Because it does not pass through the carpal tunnel, it is spared from compression, leaving thenar eminence sensation intact while digits 1-3 experience sensory loss.

options.text: The lateral antebrachial cutaneous nerve terminates prematurely at the proximal wrist crease without entering the palm
options.explanation: The lateral antebrachial cutaneous nerve (from musculocutaneous) innervates the lateral forearm skin, not the central palmar thenar eminence.

explanation: The median nerve gives off the palmar cutaneous branch approximately 5 cm proximal to the wrist crease. This branch courses superficial to the flexor retinaculum (transverse carpal ligament) to innervate the skin overlying the central thenar eminence. Because it does not pass through the carpal tunnel, it is spared from compression, leaving thenar eminence sensation intact while digits 1-3 experience sensory loss. Carpal tunnel with preserved thenar sensation = Palmar cutaneous branch arises proximal to carpal tunnel and passes superficial to flexor retinaculum.

subject: Biochemistry
topic: Scurvy Collagen Post-Translational Hydroxylation Defect
stem: A 68-year-old widower who lives alone on an unvarying diet of canned tea and white toast presents to the clinic with progressive fatigue, spontaneous bruising, and painful swelling of his knees. Physical examination demonstrates pale conjunctivae, swollen spongy purple gums that bleed readily upon probing, petechiae centered around hair follicles with corkscrew hairs on both lower extremities, and bilateral subperiosteal hematomas over the anterior tibiae. Laboratory evaluation reveals a normocytic anemia and normal platelet count (240,000/mm3) with normal coagulation studies (PT and PTT normal). Which of the following post-translational enzymatic reactions is directly impaired in this patient?

options.text: Extracellular oxidative deamination of lysine and hydroxylysine residues by copper-dependent lysyl oxidase
options.explanation: Lysyl oxidase cross-links tropocollagen extracellularly using copper as a cofactor; deficiency causes Menkes disease or lathyrism, not vitamin C-dependent scurvy.

options.text: Addition of glucose and galactose residues to hydroxylysine by endoplasmic reticulum glycosyltransferases
options.explanation: Glycosylation of hydroxylysine residues does not require vitamin C as a cofactor; hydroxylation must precede glycosylation.

options.text: Proteolytic cleavage of terminal propeptides by procollagen N-proteinase in the extracellular matrix
options.explanation: Propeptide cleavage occurs extracellularly and is independent of ascorbic acid; defects cause Ehlers-Danlos syndrome arthrochalasia type.

options.text: Gamma-carboxylation of glutamic acid residues in procollagen monomers catalyzed by vitamin K-dependent carboxylase
options.explanation: Vitamin K mediates gamma-carboxylation of clotting factors (II, VII, IX, X) and osteocalcin, not collagen alpha chains.

options.text: Hydroxylation of specific proline and lysine residues within the rough endoplasmic reticulum, catalyzed by prolyl and lysyl hydroxylases requiring ferrous iron and ascorbic acid
options.explanation: Scurvy is caused by vitamin C (ascorbic acid) deficiency. Ascorbic acid acts as a reducing agent to keep iron in its active ferrous (Fe2+) state during the catalytic cycle of prolyl and lysyl hydroxylases within the rough endoplasmic reticulum. Hydroxyproline is essential for interchain hydrogen bonding that stabilizes the collagen triple helix; deficiency yields unstable collagen that degrades at physiological temperature, causing capillary fragility (petechiae, bleeding gums) and impaired wound healing.

explanation: Scurvy is caused by vitamin C (ascorbic acid) deficiency. Hydroxyproline is essential for interchain hydrogen bonding that stabilizes the collagen triple helix; deficiency yields unstable collagen that degrades at physiological temperature, causing capillary fragility (petechiae, bleeding gums) and impaired wound healing. Tea and toast diet + bleeding gums + corkscrew hairs + petechiae = Scurvy -> Vitamin C deficiency impairs prolyl/lysyl hydroxylase in RER.
